**[TENANT ESTOPPEL CERTIFICATE]{.underline}**

Date: June 4, 2025

To:

**Prairieview Holdings LLC**, an Illinois limited liability company (\"Landlord\")

**Whitfield Capital Partners LLC**, a Delaware limited liability company (\"Buyer\")

**Great Lakes Commercial Lending Corp.**, an Illinois corporation (\"Lender\")

and their respective successors and assigns

Re: Lease dated March 1, 2020 (the \"Lease\") between Prairieview Holdings LLC, as Landlord, and Meridian Analytics Inc., a Delaware corporation, as Tenant, for Floors 10, 11, and 12 of the building commonly known as Lakeshore Tower, located at 2900 Lakeshore Boulevard, Chicago, Illinois 60614 (the \"Property\")

Meridian Analytics Inc., a Delaware corporation (\"Tenant\"), hereby certifies to Landlord, Buyer, Lender, and their respective successors and assigns, as follows. Tenant understands that Buyer is acquiring the Property from Landlord and that Lender is providing financing for such acquisition. Tenant further understands and acknowledges that Buyer and Lender are relying upon the truth and accuracy of the statements made herein in connection with such acquisition and financing. The undersigned individual is duly authorized to execute and deliver this Tenant Estoppel Certificate on behalf of Tenant.

**1. Lease Identification.** The Lease was executed on or about March 1, 2020, between Landlord and Tenant. The Lease has not been amended, modified, supplemented, or otherwise changed, whether orally or in writing, since its original execution. There are no side letters, memoranda of understanding, or other agreements between Landlord and Tenant that modify, amend, or supplement the terms of the Lease. The Lease constitutes the entire agreement between Landlord and Tenant with respect to the Premises (as defined below). A true, correct, and complete copy of the Lease, including all exhibits and schedules attached thereto, has been delivered to Buyer.

**2. Premises and Term.** Pursuant to the Lease, Tenant leases Floors 10, 11, and 12 of the Property, consisting of approximately 42,600 net rentable square feet (\"NRS\") (collectively, the \"Premises\"). The Lease commencement date was March 1, 2020 (the \"Commencement Date\"). The Lease expiration date is February 28, 2030 (the \"Expiration Date\"). Tenant is currently in occupancy of the entire Premises and has accepted the Premises in their current condition. All conditions to the commencement of the Lease term have been satisfied, and the Lease term has not been extended or renewed as of the date hereof.

**3. Rent.** The current monthly base rent payable under the Lease is **\$172,175.00 per month**. Base rent is payable in equal monthly installments on the first day of each calendar month, in advance, without notice, demand, setoff, or deduction. Base rent has been paid through and including the month of June 2025. There are no free rent periods, rent abatements, rent concessions, or other rent credits currently in effect under the Lease or otherwise applicable to any future period. No rent has been prepaid more than one (1) month in advance. Tenant has not been granted any rental reduction, deferral, or forgiveness that is not expressly set forth in the Lease.

**4. Additional Rent and Operating Expenses.** In addition to base rent, Tenant is obligated to pay its proportionate share of operating expenses, real estate taxes, and insurance premiums for the Property in excess of the base year amounts established under the Lease, as additional rent. Tenant\'s proportionate share, as determined under the Lease, is approximately **21.73%** (calculated as 42,600 NRS / 196,000 total NRS for the Property). The base year for purposes of calculating Tenant\'s proportionate share of operating expenses is calendar year 2020. All additional rent obligations have been paid current through the most recent billing period for which invoices have been received by Tenant. As of the date hereof, there are no disputes, claims, or objections pending between Landlord and Tenant regarding any operating expense reconciliation, pass-through calculation, or additional rent invoice.

**5. Security Deposit.** Tenant has deposited with Landlord a security deposit in the form of an irrevocable standby letter of credit in the amount of **\$344,350.00**, issued by Calverley State Bank, Letter of Credit No. BW-2020-4471 (the \"Letter of Credit\"). The Letter of Credit is currently in full force and effect and has not been drawn upon, in whole or in part. The current expiration date of the Letter of Credit is March 30, 2030, which is at least thirty (30) days beyond the Lease Expiration Date. The Letter of Credit contains customary auto-renewal provisions and will automatically renew for successive one-year periods unless the issuing bank provides written notice of non-renewal not fewer than sixty (60) days prior to the then-current expiration date.

**6. Tenant Improvement Allowance.** Pursuant to the Lease, Landlord agreed to provide Tenant with a tenant improvement allowance in the amount of **\$65.00 per NRS**, for a total tenant improvement allowance of **\$2,769,000.00**. The tenant improvement allowance has been fully disbursed by Landlord, and Tenant has received all funds to which it is entitled under the Lease with respect to tenant improvements. Tenant has no outstanding claims, requests, or demands for additional tenant improvement funds or reimbursements. All tenant improvements contemplated under the Lease have been completed and accepted by Tenant.

**7. Options and Preferential Rights.** Tenant has two (2) five-year renewal options (each, a \"Renewal Option\") pursuant to the terms of the Lease. Each Renewal Option permits Tenant to extend the Lease term for an additional period of five (5) years at a rental rate equal to ninety-five percent (95%) of the then-prevailing fair market rental rate for comparable space in the relevant market area, as determined in accordance with the procedures set forth in the Lease. Each Renewal Option is exercisable upon written notice delivered by Tenant to Landlord not less than twelve (12) months prior to the expiration of the then-current Lease term (or renewal term, as applicable). As of the date hereof, neither Renewal Option has been exercised by Tenant.

**8. Defaults and Disputes.** To Tenant\'s knowledge, neither Tenant nor Landlord is currently in default under any of the terms, covenants, or conditions of the Lease, and no event has occurred and no condition exists that, with the giving of notice or the passage of time, or both, would constitute a default by either Tenant or Landlord under the Lease. There is no existing claim, defense, offset, or counterclaim that Tenant has or claims to have against Landlord arising out of or in connection with the Lease, the Premises, or the Property. There are no actions, suits, proceedings, or claims pending or, to Tenant\'s knowledge, threatened against or by Tenant before any court, governmental authority, arbitrator, or other tribunal that would adversely affect Tenant\'s ability to perform its obligations under the Lease or that relate in any way to the Lease or the Premises.

**9. Subleases and Assignments.** Tenant has not assigned, transferred, pledged, hypothecated, or otherwise encumbered the Lease or any interest therein, and Tenant has not sublet any portion of the Premises. No third party has any right to occupy or use any portion of the Premises other than Tenant.

**10. Parking.** Tenant has forty (40) reserved parking spaces in the Property\'s parking garage pursuant to the terms of the Lease. The current rate for such parking spaces is **\$225.00 per space per month**, for a total monthly parking charge of **\$9,000.00**. All parking charges are current as of the date hereof.

**11. Miscellaneous Certifications.** Tenant makes the following additional certifications as of the date hereof:

> \(a\) Tenant has not filed, and is not the subject of, any petition under the federal bankruptcy laws of the United States (Title 11 of the United States Code), or any state insolvency, receivership, reorganization, or similar debtor-relief laws. No assignment for the benefit of creditors has been made by Tenant, and no receiver, trustee, or custodian has been appointed for, or has taken possession of, all or substantially all of Tenant\'s assets.
>
> \(b\) Tenant has not received any notice of condemnation, eminent domain, or similar proceedings affecting the Premises or any portion of the Property.
>
> \(c\) To Tenant\'s knowledge, no hazardous materials, substances, or wastes (as defined under any applicable federal, state, or local environmental law, regulation, or ordinance) have been generated, used, stored, treated, released, or disposed of by Tenant at, on, under, or about the Premises in violation of any applicable environmental laws.
>
> \(d\) The Lease is in full force and effect and has not been terminated, cancelled, or surrendered. The Lease, as identified in Section 1 above, represents the entire agreement between Landlord and Tenant with respect to the Premises.
>
> \(e\) This Tenant Estoppel Certificate may be relied upon by Landlord, Buyer, Lender, and each of their respective successors, assigns, transferees, and designees.

**12. Reliance and Binding Effect.** Tenant acknowledges that this Tenant Estoppel Certificate is being delivered to Buyer and Lender in connection with Buyer\'s acquisition of the Property from Landlord and Lender\'s financing of such acquisition, and that Buyer and Lender will rely on the truth, accuracy, and completeness of the certifications and statements contained herein in consummating such acquisition and financing. This Tenant Estoppel Certificate shall be binding upon Tenant and its successors and assigns and shall inure to the benefit of Landlord, Buyer, Lender, and their respective successors, assigns, and designees. The statements contained in this Tenant Estoppel Certificate are true, correct, and complete in all material respects as of the date first written above.

*\[Signature Page Follows\]*

*\[Signature Page to Tenant Estoppel Certificate\]*

**TENANT:**

**MERIDIAN ANALYTICS INC.**, a Delaware corporation

By: **\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_**

Name: David Pham

Title: Vice President, Real Estate

Date: June 4, 2025

**[TENANT ESTOPPEL CERTIFICATE]{.underline}**

**Lakeview Legal Group LLP --- Floors 7 and 8, 2900 Lakeshore Boulevard, Chicago, Illinois 60614**

Dated: June 5, 2025

The undersigned, **Lakeview Legal Group LLP**, an Illinois limited liability partnership (\"Tenant\"), hereby certifies, represents, and warrants the following to **Whitfield Capital Partners LLC**, a Delaware limited liability company (\"Buyer\"), and **Great Lakes Commercial Lending Corp.**, an Illinois corporation (\"Lender\"), and to their respective successors and assigns, in connection with Buyer\'s proposed acquisition of the property commonly known as Lakeshore Tower, located at 2900 Lakeshore Boulevard, Chicago, Illinois 60614 (the \"Property\"), which Property is currently owned by **Prairieview Holdings LLC**, an Illinois limited liability company (\"Landlord\"). Tenant understands and acknowledges that Buyer and Lender, and their respective successors and assigns, will rely upon the statements, representations, and certifications contained in this Certificate in connection with the purchase, financing, and underwriting of the Property. Tenant makes the following certifications as of the date first written above:

**[1. Lease Identification]{.underline}**

Tenant is party to that certain Office Lease Agreement dated September 1, 2018 (the \"Lease\") entered into between Landlord, as landlord, and Tenant, as tenant, for premises consisting of the entirety of Floors 7 and 8 of the building located at 2900 Lakeshore Boulevard, Chicago, Illinois 60614 (the \"Building\"), comprising approximately 28,400 net rentable square feet (\"NRS\") (the \"Premises\"). The Lease has not been amended, modified, supplemented, or otherwise changed, whether orally or in writing, except as follows: **None.** There are no side letters, oral agreements, memoranda of understanding, or other written or unwritten understandings between Tenant and Landlord that in any way modify, supplement, or affect the terms, covenants, or conditions of the Lease. A true, correct, and complete copy of the Lease, together with all exhibits and attachments thereto, has been previously delivered to Landlord and is available to Buyer and Lender upon request.

**[2. Lease Term]{.underline}**

The commencement date of the Lease is **September 1, 2018**. The scheduled expiration date of the Lease is **August 31, 2028**, unless sooner terminated or extended in accordance with the terms of the Lease. The current lease year is Year 7, running from September 1, 2024 through August 31, 2025. Tenant is currently in occupancy of the Premises and has been in continuous, uninterrupted occupancy since the lease commencement date. Pursuant to the terms of the Lease, Tenant has **one (1) five-year renewal option** at fair market rent, exercisable upon delivery of not less than **twelve (12) months\' advance written notice** to Landlord prior to the expiration of the then-current Lease term. As of the date of this Certificate, Tenant has not exercised this renewal option, and the period within which to exercise the renewal option has not yet expired.

**[3. Rent]{.underline}**

The base rent payable under the Lease is structured as follows:

  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Lease Years**                                **Rate per NRS per Year**   **Annual Base Rent**   **Monthly Base Rent**
  ---------------------------------------------- --------------------------- ---------------------- -----------------------
  Years 1--5 (Sept. 1, 2018 -- Aug. 31, 2023)    \$44.00                     \$1,249,600.00         \$104,133.33

  Years 6--10 (Sept. 1, 2023 -- Aug. 31, 2028)   \$47.50                     \$1,349,000.00         \$112,416.67
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The current base rent rate applicable to the Premises is **\$47.50 per NRS per year**, which rate is in effect for lease years 6 through 10. Accordingly, the current monthly base rent obligation is **\$112,416.67** per month (calculated as 28,400 NRS × \$47.50 per NRS per year ÷ 12 months), and the current annual base rent obligation is **\$1,349,000.00** per year (calculated as 28,400 NRS × \$47.50 per NRS per year). Rent is due and payable on the first day of each calendar month, in advance, without demand, offset, or deduction, except as may otherwise be provided in the Lease and as may be applicable in connection with Landlord\'s breach described in Section 6 below. All rent and additional rent due under the Lease has been paid through **June 2025**. No rent or additional rent has been prepaid more than one (1) month in advance of the date on which such payment was due.

**[4. Security Deposit]{.underline}**

Landlord currently holds a cash security deposit in the amount of **\$112,417.00** pursuant to the terms of the Lease. To the best of Tenant\'s knowledge, no portion of the security deposit has been applied by Landlord against rent, additional rent, or any other charges or obligations under the Lease. Tenant has not received any notice from Landlord of any claim against or draw upon the security deposit.

**[5. Tenant Improvement Allowance]{.underline}**

Under the terms of the Lease, Landlord agreed to provide Tenant with a tenant improvement allowance in the amount of **\$55.00 per NRS**, for a total tenant improvement allowance of **\$1,562,000.00** (calculated as 28,400 NRS × \$55.00 per NRS). As of the date of this Certificate, the tenant improvement allowance has been **fully disbursed** by Landlord, and Tenant has no outstanding claims, requests, or demands for additional tenant improvement funds or any other construction-related allowances or reimbursements under the Lease.

**[6. Exclusive Use]{.underline}**

Pursuant to **Section 8.5** of the Lease, Landlord covenanted and agreed that Landlord would not lease, sublease, license, or otherwise permit any other space in the Building to be occupied or used by any law firm, legal services provider, or any entity primarily engaged in the practice of law or the provision of legal services (the \"Exclusive Use Restriction\"). The Exclusive Use Restriction runs for the full term of the Lease, including any renewal or extension thereof.

Tenant hereby notifies Buyer and Lender that Landlord is currently in violation of the Exclusive Use Restriction set forth in Section 8.5 of the Lease. Specifically, in or about January 2025, Atlas Compliance Solutions LLP, an entity that Tenant understands to be a legal services provider, commenced occupancy of Suite 510 on Floor 5 of the Building. Tenant notified Landlord\'s property manager, Graystone Property Services Inc., of this violation in writing on or about February 10, 2025, and again on March 18, 2025. As of the date of this Certificate, Landlord has not cured this breach or provided any substantive response to Tenant\'s written notices. Tenant expressly reserves all rights and remedies available to it under the Lease and at law or in equity with respect to Landlord\'s breach of Section 8.5, including without limitation any rights to rent abatement, offset, or termination as may be provided under the Lease or applicable law.

**[7. Parking]{.underline}**

Pursuant to the Lease, Tenant has the right to use **25 reserved parking spaces** in the Building\'s parking garage at a current rate of **\$225.00 per space per month**, for a total monthly parking charge of **\$5,625.00** (calculated as 25 spaces × \$225.00 per space per month). All parking charges are current and have been paid through **June 2025**.

**[8. Defaults and Disputes]{.underline}**

**Tenant\'s Defaults.** Tenant certifies that, to the best of Tenant\'s knowledge and as of the date of this Certificate, Tenant is not in default under any provision of the Lease, and no event has occurred and no condition exists which, with the giving of notice or the passage of time, or both, would constitute a default by Tenant under the Lease. Tenant has not received any notice of default from Landlord that remains uncured.

**Landlord\'s Defaults.** Tenant certifies that, except as set forth in Section 6 above regarding Landlord\'s breach of the Exclusive Use Restriction contained in Section 8.5 of the Lease, to the best of Tenant\'s knowledge, Landlord has performed all material obligations required to be performed by Landlord under the Lease through the date hereof, and Tenant has not delivered to Landlord any notice of default that remains uncured other than the notices described in Section 6 above relating to the Exclusive Use Restriction.

**[9. Subleases and Assignments]{.underline}**

Tenant has not assigned the Lease or any interest therein to any person or entity. Tenant has not sublet, subleased, or otherwise transferred the right to occupy any portion of the Premises to any third party. No person or entity other than Tenant has any right to occupy or is currently occupying any portion of the Premises.

**[10. Right of First Refusal / Right of First Offer]{.underline}**

The Lease does not grant Tenant any right of first refusal, right of first offer, expansion option, or similar preferential right with respect to any other space in the Building or the Property. Tenant has no contractual right under the Lease to lease, occupy, or acquire any space in the Building other than the Premises.

**[11. Miscellaneous Certifications]{.underline}**

Tenant hereby further certifies and represents as follows:

> \(a\) Tenant has no right to any rent-free period, rent concession, or rent abatement currently in effect under the Lease, except as may arise from or be applicable in connection with Landlord\'s breach of the Exclusive Use Restriction described in Section 6 above.
>
> \(b\) The Lease represents the entire agreement between Tenant and Landlord with respect to the leasing, use, and occupancy of the Premises, and there are no agreements, whether oral or written, between Tenant and Landlord with respect to the Premises other than the Lease as identified in Section 1 above.
>
> \(c\) No bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, receivership, or similar proceedings have been commenced by or against Tenant, and Tenant is not contemplating the filing of any such proceeding.
>
> \(d\) Tenant has received no notice of any condemnation, eminent domain, or governmental taking proceedings affecting the Property or the Premises or any portion thereof.
>
> \(e\) Tenant has not received notice of any hazardous materials, environmental contamination, or environmental conditions affecting the Premises or the Building that would materially impair Tenant\'s use or occupancy of the Premises.
>
> \(f\) The Lease is in full force and effect and has not been terminated, canceled, or surrendered, and Tenant has no present intention to terminate the Lease prior to the scheduled expiration date.

**[12. Reliance]{.underline}**

This Certificate is made with the understanding and acknowledgment that Whitfield Capital Partners LLC and Great Lakes Commercial Lending Corp., and their respective successors and assigns, will rely upon the certifications, representations, and statements made herein in connection with the acquisition, ownership, and financing of the Property. This Certificate shall inure to the benefit of and be binding upon Tenant and its successors and assigns, and upon any party that acquires an interest in the Property or any mortgage or deed of trust encumbering the Property in reliance upon this Certificate. This Certificate shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Illinois, without regard to conflicts of law principles.

**IN WITNESS WHEREOF**, the undersigned has executed this Tenant Estoppel Certificate as of the date first written above.

**LAKEVIEW LEGAL GROUP LLP**, an Illinois limited liability partnership

doc.add_heading('I.  Executive summary and bottom line', level=1)

para('Seller has delivered five tenant estoppel certificates \u2014 from Meridian Analytics Inc., Lakeview Legal Group LLP, '

     'Our review of the five certificates against the lease abstracts, the May 31, 2025 rent roll and the PSA yields six '
     'conclusions.', after=6, align='j')

numbered(1, '**The estoppel condition cannot be satisfied by these five certificates. **PSA \u00a7 7.1(c) requires '
            'certificates from tenants occupying not less than 75% of building NRS (147,000 NRS). Five certificates '
            'covering 65.20% leave a shortfall of 19,200 NRS. [CHECK \u2014 App. B, B-12] Even if every certificate were '
            'perfect, the threshold fails by more than one full floor of leased space.')
numbered(2, '**Every certificate fails the 30-day recency requirement. **Each must be dated no earlier than 30 days '
            'before the Closing Date: on or after July 16, 2025 for an August 15, 2025 closing. All five are dated June 3\u20135, '
            '2025 \u2014 71 to 73 days before closing and 41 to 43 days before the earliest permissible date. '
            '[CHECK \u2014 App. B, B-13] None can be relied on for the condition as presently dated.')

            'landlord defaults and monetised tenant claims; re-certification alone will not produce the unconditional '
            'certifications that PSA \u00a7 7.1(c)(iv)\u2013(v) requires.')

            'All of this sits inside a $3,000,000 rep cap with a 12-month survival period that does not cover post-closing '
            'operating losses (PSA \u00a7 5.6).')
numbered(6, '**There is a timing trap in the PSA that Buyer must address now. **Buyer\u2019s due diligence election falls '
            'on July 18, 2025; compliant estoppels cannot exist before July 16, 2025; and the estoppel election date is '
            'August 8, 2025. Buyer will therefore be asked to let the due diligence period lapse before it can possibly '
            'hold compliant certificates. [CHECK \u2014 App. B, B-13, B-14]')

para('', after=4, size=2)
callout('BOTTOM LINE.',
        'Treat PSA \u00a7 7.1(c) as unsatisfied today and as incapable of satisfaction by the five certificates on file. '
        'Require (i) execution and re-issuance of all five certificates dated on or after July 16, 2025; (ii) estoppels '
        'from Atlas, Brightmark and Crestline (21,300 NRS, taking coverage to 149,100 NRS / 76.07%); (iii) Seller cure or '
        'monetary protection for the Lakeview exclusive-use breach and the NorthPoint abatement; and (iv) production of '
        'the Hartwell First Amendment with a full re-audit of Seller\u2019s lease files. Do not waive \u00a7 7.1(c) and do not '
        'let the due diligence period expire without a written reservation. See Part VIII for the action plan and Part IX '
        'for the documents required.')

doc.add_heading('Issue register', level=2)
para('Issue identifiers are used throughout this memorandum. \u201cGating\u201d means the issue can prevent satisfaction '
     'of a PSA closing condition or requires a Buyer election.', size=9.2, after=4)

rows = [
 ('A1','Estoppel coverage 127,800 NRS (65.20%) against a 147,000 NRS (75%) requirement','Critical','Yes','All five','PSA \u00a7 7.1(c); Rent Roll'),

 ('B1','Lakeview: uncured landlord default under building-wide exclusive-use covenant (Atlas, Suite 510)','Critical','Yes','Lakeview','Estoppel \u00a7 6; Abstract \u00a7 2.7; PSA \u00a7\u00a7 5.3(b), 5.4'),

 ('D3','Cascade: denial of the Pinecrest Studios sublease that Seller disclosed','High','Yes','Cascade','Estoppel \u00a7 8; PSA Ex. F item 4; Abstract \u00a7 4.8'),
 ('E1','Hartwell: undisclosed First Amendment (term to Mar 31, 2030 and Floor 13 ROFO)','Critical','Yes','Hartwell','Estoppel \u00a7\u00a7 1, 3, 7; PSA \u00a7 5.3(e); Ex. F item 5'),
 ('E2','Competing preferential rights over Floor 13 (Meridian ROFO and Hartwell ROFO); Keystone suite','High','No','Hartwell / Meridian','Abstract \u00a7\u00a7 1.7, 5.7; Rent Roll'),
 ('E3','Hartwell: security deposit $78,000 vs $65,000','Medium','No','Hartwell','Estoppel \u00a7 5; PSA \u00a7 5.3(g)'),
 ('F1','Meridian: monthly base rent understated at $172,175.00 (Year 1 rate) instead of $197,167.00','High','No','Meridian','Estoppel \u00a7 3; Abstract \u00a7 1.3; Rent Roll'),
 ('F2','Meridian: certificate silent on the Floor 13\u201314 ROFO','Medium','No','Meridian','Estoppel \u00a7 7; Abstract \u00a7 1.7'),
 ('F3','Meridian: letter of credit expires 30 days after lease expiry, not the required 60','Medium','No','Meridian','Estoppel \u00a7 5; Abstract \u00a7 1.4'),
 ('G1','Rent roll: smaller-tenant NRS foot to 52,344 vs stated 51,244; occupancy 91.9% vs 91.3%','Medium','No','\u2014','Rent Roll; PSA \u00a7 5.3(a)'),
 ('G2','Rent roll: Floor 5 and Floor 13 suite NRS exceed the 14,200 plate; \u201cfull floor\u201d Suite 1300','Medium','No','\u2014','Rent Roll, Vacant Suites'),
 ('G3','Abstract and rent roll are stale on Cascade rent and Hartwell term and deposit','High','No','\u2014','Abstract; Rent Roll'),
 ('G4','Document-control defects (counsel name, ROFO section references, consent dates, rounding)','Low','No','\u2014','Abstract; PSA Ex. F; Rent Roll'),
]
table(['ID','Issue','Severity','Gating','Certificate(s)','Principal source'],
      rows, [0.42, 2.72, 0.62, 0.55, 0.85, 1.34], font=8.0, sev_col=2, after=8)

doc.add_heading('II.  Scope, sources reviewed and method', level=1)

doc.add_heading('II.1  Documents reviewed', level=2)
rows = [
 ('Purchase and Sale Agreement, dated June 2, 2025 \u2014 excerpts (Art. 5, Art. 7, Exhibit F)','PSA','Seller-representation, condition, estoppel-form and disclosure framework'),
 ('Lease Abstract Summary, prepared by Seller\u2019s counsel, dated June 1, 2025 \u2014 five major tenants','Abstract','Secondary summary of lease terms (not the leases)'),
 ('Rent Roll as of May 31, 2025, prepared by Graystone Property Services Inc. (\u201cRent Roll\u201d)','Rent Roll','Occupancy, rent, deposit, TI and parking data; four tabs'),
 ('Tenant Estoppel Certificate \u2014 Meridian Analytics Inc., dated June 4, 2025','Meridian','Subject of review'),
 ('Tenant Estoppel Certificate \u2014 Lakeview Legal Group LLP, dated June 5, 2025','Lakeview','Subject of review'),
 ('Tenant Estoppel Certificate \u2014 NorthPoint Financial Advisors LLC, dated June 4, 2025','NorthPoint','Subject of review'),
 ('Tenant Estoppel Certificate \u2014 Cascade Digital Media Corp., dated June 3, 2025','Cascade','Subject of review'),
 ('Tenant Estoppel Certificate \u2014 Hartwell & Burke Consulting Inc., dated June 5, 2025','Hartwell','Subject of review'),
]
table(['Document','Short cite','Use in this memorandum'], rows, [3.05, 0.85, 2.60], font=8.4, after=8)

doc.add_heading('II.2  Method', level=2)
para('We did four things. First, we extracted from each certificate every factual certification capable of being tested \u2014 '
     'parties, premises, commencement and expiration, current rent, security deposit, tenant improvement allowance, '
     'options and preferential rights, subleases, defaults, claims and offsets, and parking \u2014 and reduced each to a '
     'discrete field. Second, we populated the same fields from the Abstract, the Rent Roll and the PSA so that every '
     'field had four independent sources. Third, we recomputed every rent schedule, pro rata share, subtotal and '
     'threshold arithmetically, and recomputed every date interval, rather than accepting stated totals; those '
     'computations are set out in Appendices A and B. Fourth, we tested each discrepancy against the specific PSA '
     'representation or condition it touches, so that the memorandum identifies not merely that documents differ but '
     'which contractual protection is engaged. [CHECK \u2014 Appendices A and B]', align='j')

doc.add_heading('II.3  What we could not verify', level=2)
para('Three limits apply to everything that follows, and we have not cured them by assumption.', after=3)
bullet('**The underlying leases were not provided.** The Abstract is a Seller-prepared secondary summary that states on '
       'its face that the lease documents control. Every lease-term finding in this memorandum is therefore a finding '
       'that the certificate is inconsistent with Seller\u2019s own summary, not a finding about what the lease says.')
bullet('**The PSA is an excerpt.** Articles 1\u20134 and 6\u201312, Exhibit B (Permitted Exceptions), Exhibit E (lease schedule), '

       'signature, initials or date adjacent to it. If executed originals exist, that cures issue A3 only, and changes '
       'nothing else.')

para('**The covenant.** Abstract \u00a7 2.7 records that under lease \u00a7 8.5 Landlord covenanted not to lease space in the '
     'building \u201cto any other law firm or entity primarily engaged in the practice of law,\u201d that the restriction applies '

     'abatement of up to 10% of monthly base rent per month of violation, and actual damages \u2014 are cumulative. The '
     'tenant\u2019s own statement of the covenant (Estoppel \u00a7 6) is materially identical. There is therefore no dispute '
     'about the existence or scope of the covenant. [FACT \u2014 Abstract \u00a7 2.7; Lakeview Estoppel \u00a7 6]', align='j')
para('**The breach.** Lakeview states that Atlas Compliance Solutions LLP, \u201can entity that Tenant understands to be a '
     'legal services provider,\u201d commenced occupancy of Suite 510 on Floor 5 in or about January 2025; that it notified '

     'Landlord has neither cured the breach nor substantively responded. The Rent Roll independently describes Atlas as a '
     '\u201cLegal/compliance services provider\u201d with occupancy commencing January 2025. [FACT \u2014 Lakeview Estoppel \u00a7 6; '
     'Rent Roll, \u201cSmaller Tenants Detail\u201d]', align='j')
para('**Why this defeats Seller\u2019s representations.** Both notices predate the June 2, 2025 Effective Date by roughly four '
     'months. PSA \u00a7 5.3(b) represents that \u201cSeller has not received written notice from any tenant alleging any such '
     'default\u201d and that no tenant has \u201casserted any claim, offset, defense, or counterclaim.\u201d PSA \u00a7 5.4 represents '
     'that no \u201cwritten demand, notice of claim, or notice of intent to commence legal proceedings from any tenant\u201d '
     'remains unresolved and that Seller is not party to any settlement with a tenant. PSA \u00a7 5.4 also represents that '

     'were given to the managing agent identified in the Abstract as the Property manager, and PSA \u00a7 5.3(c) expressly '

     'current instrument does not satisfy it. [FACT \u2014 Meridian Estoppel \u00b6 5; Abstract \u00a7 1.4] [CHECK \u2014 App. B, B-10]',
     align='j')
para('Separately, PSA \u00a7 5.3(g) requires Seller at Closing to deliver \u201cevidence of the current status and validity of '

     'Bank.\u201d The certificate is not that evidence. Buyer needs the instrument itself, the bank\u2019s current-status letter, '
     'confirmation that the LOC is transferable and will be re-issued or amended in Buyer\u2019s name, and an allocation of '
     'any bank fee \u2014 failing which Buyer should require a cash replacement deposit or a $344,350 closing credit. A '
     'letter of credit is the only security deposit in the building that cannot simply be credited at Closing, and it is '
     'the only one that can evaporate if the mechanics are left to closing day.', align='j')

doc.add_heading('Recommended actions', level=3)
numbered(1, '**Re-certify with the correct rent**: $197,167.00 per month, $55.54/NRS, $2,366,004 per year, and confirm the '
            '2.75% compounding escalation and the Year 6 period.')
numbered(2, '**Add ROFO disclosure**: existence and terms, whether it was triggered by the Keystone Suite 1310 lease or by '
            'any prior marketing of Floor 13/14, whether Meridian asserts any claim, and whether it will waive or '
            'subordinate the right for Suite 1300 if Buyer needs that space leasable.')
numbered(3, '**Reconcile the ROFO section reference** (\u00a7 10.4 per the Abstract, \u00a7 6.4 per the Rent Roll) from the lease '
            'and correct the Abstract and Rent Roll.')
numbered(4, '**Lock down the letter of credit**: obtain a copy of the instrument, Calverley State Bank\u2019s current-status '
            'letter, confirmation of the required tail (30 or 60 days) from the lease, transfer/assignment documentation '
            'and fee allocation, and written confirmation that the LOC can be re-issued in Buyer\u2019s name. If it cannot, '
            'require a cash replacement deposit or a $344,350 credit at Closing.')
numbered(5, '**Obtain the Meridian Lease** to verify the ROFO, the LOC tail, the sublease profit-share and the parking '
            'provisions \u2014 all of which are material to a tenant of this size.')
PYEOF
echo ok"}

para('One structural observation follows from the matrix. The four inaccurate representations (\u00a7\u00a7 5.3(b), 5.3(c), 5.3(e) '

rows = [
 ('Smaller tenants \u2014 leased NRS','51,244','52,344','+1,100','Sum of 14 itemised rows exceeds stated subtotal'),
 ('Total leased NRS','179,044','180,144','+1,100','Propagates PSA \u00a7 5.3(a)'),
 ('Occupancy rate','91.3%','91.91%','+0.61 pts','Vacant NRS foot correctly at 16,956'),
 ('Total building NRS','196,000','197,100','+1,100','Building does not foot as presented'),

 ('Five major tenants \u2014 annual rent','$6,397,384','$6,510,984','+$113,600','Abstract uses Cascade Year 5 rate; Rent Roll does not'),

      caption='Table VI.1 \u2014 Rent Roll and Abstract: recomputation results', after=8)

doc.add_heading('VI.2  Floor-level areas exceed the plate (issue G2)', level=2)
para('Nine full-floor tenants at 14,200 NRS each account for 127,800 NRS, leaving 68,200 NRS for Floors 1, 2, 5, 9 and 13. '
     'Floor 9 foots exactly at 14,200. The others do not: Floor 5 tenancies total 17,044 NRS (Atlas 7,100 + Brightmark '

para('The commercial consequence is not the 1,100 NRS. It is that NRS drives pro rata operating-expense shares, the 75% '
     'estoppel threshold, the Lender\u2019s covenant calculations and Buyer\u2019s leasing plan for Floor 13 \u2014 where the vacancy '

     're-measurement or obtain the survey-based area schedule before Closing, and should not accept the Rent Roll\u2019s areas '

doc.add_heading('VI.4  Document-control defects (issue G4)', level=2)

     'consistent with the substantive omissions identified above.', after=3)

 ('Abstract cover vs signature block','Prepared by \u201cOakvale Strasser LLP\u201d; signed by \u201cRIDGEMONT STRASSER LLP\u201d; PSA identifies Oakvale Strasser LLP as Seller\u2019s counsel','Confirm the issuing firm; re-issue the Abstract on the correct letterhead'),

 ('Lakeview \u2014 prospective abatement to Aug. 31, 2028','Recurring, post-closing','$410,700','10% \u00d7 monthly base rent \u00d7 36.5 months'),

 ('NorthPoint \u2014 HVAC remediation capex','One-time, unquantified','TBD','Engineering report required'),
 ('NorthPoint \u2014 additional TI credit if tenant correct','One-time, contingent','$142,000','$284,000 \u2212 $142,000'),
 ('Hartwell \u2014 deposit shortfall','One-time','$13,000','$78,000 \u2212 $65,000'),
 ('Cascade \u2014 June 2025 rent shortfall','One-time','$9,467','$108,866.67 \u2212 $99,400'),
 ('Cascade \u2014 annual rent mis-stated if Abstract correct','Recurring (revenue understated)','$113,600 per year','$46.00 \u2212 $42.00 \u00d7 28,400'),
 ('Meridian \u2014 estoppel understatement','Valuation only (no cash loss)','$299,904 per year','Year 6 rent vs Year 1 rent certified'),
 ('Hartwell \u2014 term extension (favourable)','Recurring (revenue added)','\u2248 $835,000 and $856,000','Lease years 6 and 7 \u2014 Appendix A.2'),

table(['Exposure item','Character','Amount','Derivation'], rows, [2.30,1.30,0.85,2.05], font=7.6,
      caption='Table VII.1 \u2014 Consolidated exposure schedule (all amounts recomputed in Appendix B)', after=6)
para('**Aggregates.** Recurring abatement exposure is $194,900 per year at the two affected tenants. Balance-sheet and '
     'contingent items total approximately $164,467 ($142,000 + $13,000 + $9,467), excluding Lakeview\u2019s accrued abatement '
     'claim. Abatement exposure measured to each lease\u2019s expiry is approximately $744,000 ($494,200 + $249,800). Against '
     'that, PSA \u00a7 5.6 provides a $3,000,000 cap and a 12-month survival period. [CHECK \u2014 App. B, B-15 to B-19]', align='j')

doc.add_heading('VII.2  Why the rep cap does not solve the problem', level=2)
para('Two features of PSA \u00a7 5.6 make it an inadequate remedy here. First, the survival period is 12 months from Closing '
     '(to August 15, 2026), whereas the Lakeview and NorthPoint exposures are monthly obligations running to 2028. A claim '
     'for a breach discovered in 2027 is time-barred even though the cost is still being incurred. Second, the cap is '
     'aggregate: a single adverse outcome exhausts it. If Lakeview were to terminate over the \u00a7 8.5 breach, the remaining '
     'base rent from Closing to August 31, 2028 is approximately $4,110,000 \u2014 which exceeds the $3,000,000 cap before any '
     'allowance for re-letting cost, downtime or abatement. [CHECK \u2014 App. B, B-19]', align='j')
para('The recommendation that follows is therefore not a larger cap but a different instrument: a specific indemnity for '
     'the Lakeview exclusive-use matter and the NorthPoint HVAC/abatement matter, carved out of \u00a7 5.6, secured by a '
     'closing holdback or purchase-price credit sized to the exposures in Table VII.1, with a survival period running to '
     'the end of the affected lease terms rather than 12 months.', align='j')

doc.add_heading('VII.3  The \u00a7 7.1(f) material adverse change test', level=2)
para('PSA \u00a7 7.1(f) defines a material adverse change as an event that would reasonably be expected to reduce net operating '
     'income by more than 5% on an annualised basis. We do not have operating statements, so the test cannot be run '
     'precisely; but the arithmetic frame is as follows. Total annual base rent across all tenants is $8,709,917. The two '
     'abatement exposures total $194,900 per year, or 2.24% of base rent. If NOI runs at roughly 60% of base rent '
     '(\u2248 $5.2M), a 5% threshold is \u2248 $261,000, and the abatement exposures alone \u2014 at $194,900 \u2014 fall just short of it. '
     '[CHECK \u2014 App. B, B-20] [ASSUMPTION: NOI margin of 60%; actual NOI to be taken from Seller\u2019s trailing-twelve-month '
     'statement.]', align='j')
para('That is the wrong question to stop at, for two reasons. First, the NOI test captures recurring losses, not '
     'contingent ones: a Lakeview termination, or an HVAC failure that spreads beyond Floor 6, would cross the threshold '
     'immediately. Second, the clause expressly includes \u201cany \u2026 material default\u201d in the status of the Leases as a '
     'material adverse change. On that language the Lakeview default and the NorthPoint abatement are within the clause '
     'irrespective of the NOI arithmetic, and Buyer should obtain the T-12 during due diligence \u2014 before the July 18 '
     'election \u2014 so that the analysis is factual rather than structural. [CHARACTERIZATION]', align='j')
PYEOF
echo ok"}

Seller has delivered five tenant estoppel certificates — from Meridian Analytics Inc.,
Lakeview Legal Group LLP, NorthPoint Financial Advisors LLC, Cascade Digital Media
Corp. and Hartwell & Burke Consulting Inc. — dated June 3 through June 5, 2025.
Those five tenants together occupy 127,800 NRS, or 65.20% of the Property’s 196,000
NRS. Our review of the five certificates against the lease abstracts, the May 31, 2025
rent roll and the PSA yields six conclusions.
1. The estoppel condition cannot be satisfied by these five certificates. PSA §
   7.1(c) requires certificates from tenants occupying not less than 75% of building
   NRS (147,000 NRS). Five certificates covering 65.20% leave a shortfall of 19,200
   NRS. [CHECK — App. B, B-12] Even if every certificate were perfect, the threshold
   fails by more than one full floor of leased space.
2. Every certificate fails the 30-day recency requirement. Each must be dated no
   earlier than 30 days before the Closing Date: on or after July 16, 2025 for an
   August 15, 2025 closing. All five are dated June 3–5, 2025 — 71 to 73 days before
   closing and 41 to 43 days before the earliest permissible date. [CHECK — App. B,
   B-13] None can be relied on for the condition as presently dated.
3. Three of the five certificates contradict express Seller representations.
   Lakeview discloses an uncured landlord default (breach of its building-wide
   exclusive-use covenant) and reserved rights of abatement, offset and termination;
   NorthPoint discloses an undisclosed $5,000 per month rent abatement; Hartwell
   discloses a November 15, 2024 lease amendment that Seller certified on Exhibit F
   did not exist. Each squarely contradicts PSA §§ 5.3(b), 5.3(c) and/or 5.3(e) and §
   5.4.
4. Two certificates are unqualified and merely inaccurate; three are qualified,
   not merely inaccurate. The distinction matters: Meridian’s and Cascade’s
   defects (Meridian’s rent understated by $299,904 per year; Cascade’s term
   understated by two years, rent understated by $9,466.67 per month, and its
   Pinecrest sublease denied) can be cured by re-certification. The Lakeview and
   NorthPoint qualifications disclose live landlord defaults and monetised tenant
   claims; re-certification alone will not produce the unconditional certifications that
   PSA § 7.1(c)(iv)–(v) requires.
5. The monetary exposure is real but bounded. Revenue at risk is approximately
   $194,900 per year (Lakeview’s 10% abatement remedy at $134,900 per year plus
   NorthPoint’s $60,000 per year), with one-time and contingent items of
   approximately $164,467 (NorthPoint TI credit $142,000 if the tenant’s figures are
   right, Hartwell deposit $13,000, Cascade June 2025 rent $9,466.67). The cost of
   actually curing the Lakeview breach by buying out Atlas Compliance Solutions LLP
   is approximately $1.6 million before negotiation, and Lakeview also holds a
   termination right affecting 28,400 NRS (14.49% of the building). [CHECK — App.
   B, B-15 to B-17] All of this sits inside a $3,000,000 rep cap with a 12-month
   survival period that does not cover post-closing operating losses (PSA § 5.6).
6. There is a timing trap in the PSA that Buyer must address now. Buyer’s due
   diligence election falls on July 18, 2025; compliant estoppels cannot exist before

III. DO THE CERTIFICATES SATISFY PSA § 7.1(C)?
PSA § 7.1(c) imposes two independent requirements that are frequently confused: a
quantitative threshold (certificates from tenants occupying at least 75% of building
NRS) and a qualitative standard (each certificate must contain the six confirmations in
§ 7.1(c)(i)–(vi)). The certificates fail both, and they fail the threshold twice over — once
on coverage and once on dating.

III.1 Requirement A — the 75% coverage threshold (issue A1)
PSA § 7.1(c) fixes the required coverage at 147,000 NRS (75% of 196,000 NRS). The
five certificates cover 127,800 NRS. [FACT — PSA § 5.3(a); Abstract § 6; Rent Roll]
[CHECK — 127,800 ÷ 196,000 = 65.20%; 147,000 − 127,800 = 19,200 NRS shortfall;
App. B, B-12]
The shortfall is not marginal. It is 19,200 NRS — more than a full floor of the building’s
14,200 NRS plate — and it must be closed with additional smaller tenants whose
leases have not been abstracted for Buyer and whose estoppels have not been
requested. The Rent Roll’s own lender-threshold analysis reaches the same conclusion

$856,000 in lease year 7 — see the recomputed schedule in Appendix A.2. Adverse: the
Floor 13 ROFO. On a corrected record Hartwell becomes a credit-positive tenant,
which is why the correct response is to document the amendment rather than to resist
it.

The Floor 13 preferential-rights conflict (E2)
Hartwell’s ROFO (First Amendment § 2) requires Landlord to offer Floor 13 to
Hartwell “on terms no less favorable than those offered to any third party before
entering into a lease with such third party for all or any portion of the thirteenth floor.”
Meridian separately holds a right of first offer on Floors 13 and 14 under its 2020 lease
(Abstract § 1.7, citing lease § 10.4; the Rent Roll cites § 6.4 — the two references
cannot both be right), with a 15-business-day acceptance window. Seller has therefore
granted two preferential rights over the same space, the Hartwell right being junior in
time to the Meridian right. [FACT — Hartwell Estoppel ¶ 7; Abstract § 1.7; Rent Roll,
“Vacant Suites”]
This matters commercially because Floor 13 is the Property’s principal vacancy: Suite
1300, 14,200 NRS, marketed at $53.00/NRS, “Spec Suite — Move-in Ready.” Under
the Rent Roll as delivered it is described as a full floor available, yet Keystone Data
Analytics Corp. has leased Suite 1310 (3,550 NRS) on Floor 13 since August 1, 2024 —
which the Abstract (§ 1.7 note) also contradicts when it says Floor 13 is “currently
vacant.” Three separate questions follow, and none is answered by any document we
have seen: (i) which right governs Suite 1300; (ii) whether the Keystone lease
triggered Meridian’s right, since the Abstract frames the right as applying when
Landlord “intends to market Floor 13 or Floor 14 for lease to third-party tenants”; and
(iii) whether Meridian or Hartwell has asserted or waived any claim. [ASSUMPTION:
the Meridian and Hartwell lease clauses control, and neither was provided.]

Recommended actions
1. Obtain the executed First Amendment within three business days, together
   with any second amendment, side letter or amendment to any guaranty. Confirm
   signature authority (PSA § 5.1 identifies Thomas Krenshaw as Seller’s sole
   authorized Manager), execution formalities and whether any lender consent was
   required. If Seller cannot produce it, require a signed Seller statement that no
   such document exists — do not simply accept the Abstract’s silence.
2. Cure the disclosure failure. Amend Exhibit F and PSA § 5.3(e) by written
   amendment, or schedule the corrected disclosure on a Seller closing certificate
   under § 7.1(a); deliver the corrected Exhibit E/E-2. Without that, Buyer closes
   knowing that a certified representation is false and weakens its own position.
3. Fix the deposit. Require the § 9.2 proration credit at $78,000, and obtain the
   deposit ledger or bank statement proving the amount actually held. A $13,000
   shortfall is small, but a deposit representation that is wrong in exactly the amount
   implied by an undisclosed amendment is a reliable indicator of what else is wrong.
4. Obtain re-certification dated on or after July 16, 2025 stating the corrected
   expiration (March 31, 2030), the Floor 13 ROFO in full, and the correct deposit —
   ideally with a confirmation that Hartwell has not exercised and is not asserting any
   ROFO claim over the existing tenancies.
5. Resolve the ROFO priority. Obtain Meridian’s and Hartwell’s ROFO clauses;
   determine which is senior; obtain Meridian’s acknowledgement in its re-certified

{"file_path": "response.md", "content": "# Estoppel issue memorandum — Lakeshore Tower

**Deliverable:** `estoppel-issue-memorandum.docx` (~32 pp., 10 parts, 3 appendices, 22 tables)

A memorandum from Buyer's counsel (Thornbury & Levine LLP) to Whitfield Capital Partners LLC, dated June 16, 2025, reviewing the five tenant estoppel certificates against the lease abstracts, the May 31, 2025 rent roll and the PSA, with a discrepancy schedule, quantified exposure and an action plan.

## Method

Every certification in the five certificates was reduced to a field, populated from all four sources, and tested. Every rent schedule, pro rata share, subtotal, threshold and date interval was recomputed independently (Appendices A and B) rather than accepted as stated. Each discrepancy was then mapped to the specific PSA representation or closing condition it engages (Table V.1).

## Headline findings

**Threshold and timing (fatal, but fixable)**

- Coverage is 127,800 NRS = **65.20%** against the 75%/147,000 NRS requirement in PSA § 7.1(c) — a 19,200 NRS shortfall even if every certificate were perfect. Atlas + Brightmark + Crestline (21,300 NRS) is the minimum set that reaches 76.07%.
- All five certificates are dated **June 3–5, 2025**, i.e. 71–73 days before the August 15 closing against a 30-day recency requirement (earliest permissible: **July 16, 2025**). None can support the condition as dated. All five also appear unexecuted.
- Timing trap: the due diligence election is **July 18**, two days after compliant estoppels can first exist, while the estoppel election is not until **August 8**.

**Substantive (contradicting Seller's representations)**

| Tenant | Estoppel says | Seller's records say |
|---|---|---|
| Lakeview | Landlord in **uncured default** of § 8.5 building-wide exclusive-use covenant (Atlas, Suite 510); notices Feb. 10 and Mar. 18, 2025; abatement/offset/termination rights reserved | "No pending defaults," no claims, no abatements |
| NorthPoint | Undisclosed informal **$5,000/month abatement** since Nov. 2024 for HVAC failures, granted by the property manager; TI $284,000/$284,000 | "No rent abatements," "Full Rent Collected," TI $426,000/$142,000 |
| Hartwell | **First Amendment dated Nov. 15, 2024** (term extended to Mar. 31, 2030; Floor 13 ROFO); deposit $78,000 | Exhibit F item 5 "None"; abstract "no amendments"; deposit $65,000 |
| Cascade | Term **2029** (not 2031); rent **$99,400** (not $108,866.67); denies the Pinecrest sublease Seller disclosed | May 31, 2031; $108,866.67; Pinecrest sublease per Exhibit F item 4 |
| Meridian | Monthly rent **$172,175.00** (the Year 1 rate) | $197,167.00 — **$299,904/yr** understated; certificate also silent on the Floor 13–14 ROFO; LOC tail 30 days short of the stated 60 |

Documented consequences include falsified representations at PSA §§ 5.3(b), 5.3(c), 5.3(e) and 5.3(g) and § 5.4; competing Floor 13 preferential rights (Meridian 2020 vs Hartwell 2024) over the Property's largest vacancy; and a **rent roll that does not foot** (smaller-tenant NRS 52,344 vs stated 51,244; occupied 91.91% vs 91.3%; Floors 5 and 13 exceed their plate).

**Money.** Recurring revenue at risk ≈ **$194,900/yr**; abatement exposure to lease expiry ≈ **$744,000**; one-time items ≈ **$164,467**; Atlas buyout to cure the exclusive-use breach ≈ **$1.6M**. A single Lakeview termination claim (≈ $4.11M of remaining rent) exceeds the **$3M cap / 12-month survival** in § 5.6 — hence the recommendation for a specific indemnity outside the cap plus holdback or credit.

## Recommendations captured in Part VIII

Do not treat § 7.1(c) as satisfied. Obtain executed bring-down certificates dated on/after July 16, 2025 plus three additional tenant estoppels; demand the underlying leases and the Hartwell First Amendment; force an election on the NorthPoint abatement; obtain cure or a waiver-and-release from Lakeview; correct Exhibits E, E-2 and F; obtain Pinecrest estoppel/SNDA and the Meridian LOC transfer documents; notify the lender before August 8; and preserve the § 7.1(c)(A)–(C) elections with a written reservation before the July 18 due diligence deadline.

## Notes

Every finding is tied to a specific document and paragraph (Appendix C is the citation index), and facts, recomputations, assumptions, legal characterizations and recommendations are labelled separately. Limitations are stated expressly: the underlying leases, the complete PSA (including Exhibit G), title/survey materials and operating statements were not provided, so lease-term findings mean "inconsistent with Seller's own summary," and the § 7.1(f) NOI test is framed arithmetically pending the T-12.
"}
